description: Turn the rows of one database table that are new or changed into messages. Reads through a read-only DB agent under its own name, holds no database credential, tells each subscribed agent about each row, and marks a row done only after that agent confirms it. Start with help, then status.
author: Sergey Porfiriev

help.help: Find available methods and their limits.

status.help: The DB agent and table, the page size, the scan position, rows held against the window cap, a stuck row, the last poll and its error, and each subscriber's position, counts and any park.

poll.help: Read the rows after the scan position now and send what is new or changed.

reset.help: Forget every held row, position and confirmed mark, keeping the subscriptions, so each subscriber is sent every row again. Owners and Maintainers only; a damaged state file is replaced and its subscriptions are lost with it.

sub.add.help: Send each new or changed row to a queue or an agent's inbox, and send it again until the target confirms it. Every row is sent first unless replay:false, which starts at the newest row. You must be able to call the DB agent yourself.

args.name: target
args.help: Destination queue or agent; the creator's grants on it and on the DB agent are checked at add and before every send

args.name: replay
args.help: false: send only rows changed after the newest one now

sub.list.help: List your subscriptions with sent, confirmed, dropped and pending counts; Owners and Maintainers see all.

sub.delete.help: Remove one subscription and its marks. The creator, or an Owner or Maintainer, may do it.

args.name: id
args.help: The id from sub add or sub list

db.help: The read-only DB agent to read through, such as #db/orders@node.example; grant this agent only its read role there

engine.help: mysql or postgres, the DB agent's dialect

schema.help: Schema of the table; default the connection's own

table.help: The table to watch, a plain identifier

key.help: Unique key column, numeric or a timestamp

updated.help: Column the application sets on every insert and update: a timestamp, or epoch time with updated_unit

updated_unit.help: s or ms, when updated holds epoch time

columns.help: Other columns sent with each row, at most 64; key and updated are always sent

deleted.help: Soft-delete column: a row whose value equals deleted_value is sent as a delete; without it no delete is reported

deleted_value.help: The value that marks a row deleted, exactly as the database returns it: text, a whole number, true or false

max_rows.help: The DB agent's max_rows; a page is this minus a tenth, 1..10000

batch.help: Rows sent per round to one subscriber, 1..500

window_max.help: Rows held until every subscriber has them; a full window waits for the slowest, 1..100000

park_after.help: How long a subscriber may refuse or not confirm before it is parked and the others go on
